findings.highlight: to think you'd add the whole arrangement of compositions on top of that…
findings.evidenceJa: 「だいたい、二人ともなに考えてるんですか？ただでさえ準備期間も全然ないって言うのに、その上プログラムを全曲変更してしまうなんて…」
findings.explanation: Miyo is appalled that Kazusa and Youko changed every piece in the concert program despite having virtually no preparation time. The English says they added an extra full arrangement of compositions, inventing additional repertoire rather than a complete last-minute replacement; line 39 repeats the same misunderstanding.
findings.japanese:
「だいたい、二人ともなに考えてるんですか？
ただでさえ準備期間も全然ないって言うのに、
その上プログラムを全曲変更してしまうなんて…」
findings.todokanai: "What were you two thinking in the first place? It's bad enough she has had almost no preparation, but to think you'd add the whole arrangement of compositions on top of that…"

findings.highlight: After I lied about having the flu and stopped going to work, and even turned off my phone, it goes without saying that the editing department faced a lot of hardships.
findings.evidenceJa:
インフルエンザを理由に出社しなくなり、
いつしか連絡もつかなくなった俺は、
当然ながら、編集部内でかなり問題になっていた。
findings.explanation: Haruki stops attending work using influenza as the reason; 'lied about having the flu' is stronger, especially because he had genuinely been diagnosed earlier — His continued absence and later deception make use of the illness as a pretext plausible, but the bounded line does not establish the diagnosis itself was false.
findings.japanese:
インフルエンザを理由に出社しなくなり、
いつしか連絡もつかなくなった俺は、
当然ながら、編集部内でかなり問題になっていた。
findings.todokanai: After I lied about having the flu and stopped going to work, and even turned off my phone, it goes without saying that the editing department faced a lot of hardships.

findings.highlight: put the front page editing on your shoulders.
findings.evidenceJa: 「よく考えてみればお前、一年目の新入社員なんだもんな。それでメインの編集まで任せるってのは、どだい無理な話だった」
findings.explanation: Hamada says it was unreasonable to entrust a first-year employee with serving as the main or lead editor. メインの編集 is a substantive editorial role, not the task of editing a front page; the English changes Haruki's professional responsibility and why management is blamed.
findings.japanese:
「よく考えてみればお前、一年目の新入社員なんだもんな。
それでメインの編集まで任せるってのは、
どだい無理な話だった」
findings.todokanai: "When I think about it, you're on your first year here, and I went as far as to put the front page editing on your shoulders. Obviously that was too much."

findings.highlight: "We promised to be together no matter what. We promised to be together no matter how much time passed."
findings.evidenceJa:
「どこまでも一緒だって。
いつまでも二人きりだって」
findings.explanation: They promised to remain alone together forever; the English says merely together no matter how much time passes — The surrounding two-person-world language preserves exclusivity.
findings.japanese:
「どこまでも一緒だって。
いつまでも二人きりだって」
findings.todokanai: "We promised to be together no matter what. We promised to be together no matter how much time passed."

findings.highlight: Why didn't you forget about me then?
findings.evidenceJa: 「そんなの五年前からわかりきってることだろ！どうしてあの時に振りほどいてくれなかったんだよ！」
findings.explanation: Haruki asks why Kazusa did not shake him off or push him away five years ago, since she always knew how aggravating he was. The English asks why she did not forget him, replacing the decisive outward rejection he now wishes she had made with an internal erasure of memory.
findings.japanese:
「そんなの五年前からわかりきってることだろ！
どうしてあの時に振りほどいてくれなかったんだよ！」
findings.todokanai: "You've known that for these five whole years, haven't you!? Why didn't you forget about me then?"

findings.highlight: Like hell he'd be tricked so easily… by these obvious lies!
findings.evidenceJa: 「そんな…そんないい加減な嘘に騙されるもんか！あたしの気持ちを馬鹿にするのもいい加減にしろ！」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she will not be fooled by Haruki's irresponsible lie that his broken present self is the real Haruki she loves. The English switches the subject to 'he,' making Haruki the one who would not be tricked and rendering Kazusa's furious defense of her own feelings incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「そんな…そんないい加減な嘘に騙されるもんか！
あたしの気持ちを馬鹿にするのもいい加減にしろ！」
findings.todokanai: "Like hell he'd be tricked so easily… by these obvious lies! Stop belittling my feelings!"

findings.highlight: "The new guy was handed such extreme tasks that he was unable to take care of them all, and ruined his health."
findings.evidenceJa:
『新入社員が過大な仕事量と責任を負ったせいで、
処理しきれずに精神的に参ってしまった』
findings.explanation: The office believes workload and responsibility caused a mental collapse; 'ruined his health' is broader and less psychologically precise — The mistaken overwork explanation remains.
findings.japanese:
『新入社員が過大な仕事量と責任を負ったせいで、
処理しきれずに精神的に参ってしまった』
findings.todokanai: "The new guy was handed such extreme tasks that he was unable to take care of them all, and ruined his health."

findings.highlight: fed up with myself for not even trying to explain the truth, and in the end, I don't even have anyone I can apologize to.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな自分に嫌気が差し、本当の事情を説明しようにも、結局、誰も謝罪を受け入れてくれない。
findings.explanation: Disgusted with himself, Haruki does try to explain the real circumstances, but nobody will accept his apology because everyone insists on treating him gently. The English says he never tries and has nobody available to apologize to, reversing both his attempted confession and his coworkers' refusal to receive it.
findings.japanese:
そんな自分に嫌気が差し、本当の事情を説明しようにも、
結局、誰も謝罪を受け入れてくれない。
findings.todokanai: And I feel fed up with myself for not even trying to explain the truth, and in the end, I don't even have anyone I can apologize to.

findings.highlight: the difference in body temperature between us.
findings.evidenceJa: かずさとの温度差に、鈍感でいようとしてた。
findings.explanation: Haruki has tried to remain deliberately insensitive to the widening figurative temperature gap between his desperate insistence and Kazusa's resolve to send him back. The English again literalizes emotional temperature as body heat, despite no bodily-temperature contrast in this train argument.
findings.japanese: かずさとの温度差に、鈍感でいようとしてた。
findings.todokanai: I tried to ignore the difference in body temperature between us.

findings.highlight: Back to the person who can protect you properly…
findings.evidenceJa: 「お前を、ちゃんと守れる雪菜のところに…」
findings.explanation: After first referring generically to someone who can treasure Haruki, Kazusa names Setsuna as the person who can properly protect him. The English repeats the generic description and omits Setsuna's name, erasing the culmination of Kazusa's argument at the exact moment the train leaves their white world.
findings.japanese: 「お前を、ちゃんと守れる雪菜のところに…」
findings.todokanai: "Back to the person who can protect you properly…"

findings.highlight: her hidden attempt to express her guilt and regret toward the woman who's sitting right next to me
findings.evidenceJa: そして今、俺の隣で再び涙を溢れさせている彼女への、後ろめたさと悔恨混じりのカモフラージュ。
findings.explanation: Kazusa's transcendent performance is camouflage for the affair, motivated by guilt and regret toward the crying Setsuna: it constructs an alibi that a pianist at this level could not have been trysting with Haruki. The English turns concealment into a hidden attempt to communicate guilt, the opposite function from the alibi explained in lines 364–366.
findings.japanese:
そして今、俺の隣で再び涙を溢れさせている彼女への、
後ろめたさと悔恨混じりのカモフラージュ。
findings.todokanai: And it's also her hidden attempt to express her guilt and regret toward the woman who's sitting right next to me with tears overflowing in her eyes.

findings.highlight: Despite that, I'm sure that Kazusa blamed everything on herself, acknowledged her sins, and is trying to accept her punishment.
findings.evidenceJa:
それでもかずさは多分
『ああ、全部あたしのせいだな』と、
罪を認め、罰を受けようとするだろう。
findings.explanation: Haruki predicts Kazusa will accept all blame and punishment; the English partly shifts the prediction into past and present fact — Her self-blaming disposition remains.
findings.japanese:
それでもかずさは多分
『ああ、全部あたしのせいだな』と、
罪を認め、罰を受けようとするだろう。
findings.todokanai: Despite that, I'm sure that Kazusa blamed everything on herself, acknowledged her sins, and is trying to accept her punishment.

findings.highlight: You were able to lie to me.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ほら、自分に嘘をつくこと、できたじゃないか。雪菜への気持ちをごまかして、あたしを抱いてくれたじゃないか」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says Haruki proved he can lie to himself: he disguised his feelings for Setsuna and embraced Kazusa. The English says he lied to Kazusa, reversing the addressee and breaking her proposal that he now perform the same self-deception in the other direction for Setsuna.
findings.japanese:
「ほら、自分に嘘をつくこと、できたじゃないか。
雪菜への気持ちをごまかして、
あたしを抱いてくれたじゃないか」
findings.todokanai: "See? You were able to lie to me. You were able to trick me regarding your feelings for Setsuna, and made love to me instead."

findings.highlight: Because I finally understood that I can't bring myself to contradict Kazusa's resolve.
findings.evidenceJa:
わかってしまったから。
かずさの覚悟を翻すことができないって。
findings.explanation: Haruki understands he cannot overturn Kazusa's resolve; 'can't bring myself to contradict' makes it a failure of will rather than efficacy — The finality of her resolve remains.
findings.japanese:
わかってしまったから。
かずさの覚悟を翻すことができないって。
findings.todokanai: Because I finally understood that I can't bring myself to contradict Kazusa's resolve.

findings.highlight: I bet she's dying to applaud herself
findings.evidenceJa: きっと、すごく拍手したいはずなのに、それでも、俺を気にかけることを優先する。
findings.explanation: Setsuna must desperately want to applaud Kazusa, yet prioritizes caring for Haruki and keeps both hands occupied with him. 'Applaud herself' means self-congratulation, replacing the very admiration for Kazusa that makes Setsuna's sacrifice of applause moving.
findings.japanese:
きっと、すごく拍手したいはずなのに、
それでも、俺を気にかけることを優先する。
findings.todokanai: I bet she's dying to applaud herself, but she's prioritizing watching over me.

findings.highlight: The boundless kindness Setsuna has is deceiving Setsuna herself
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜の、その尽きない優しさこそが、雪菜を騙し、裏切ろうとする暗い心を呼び覚ます。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's inexhaustible kindness awakens in Haruki the dark impulse to deceive and betray Setsuna by accepting rescue without confessing. The English makes Setsuna's kindness itself deceive Setsuna, misattaching the action that belongs to Haruki's newly awakened dark heart.
findings.japanese:
雪菜の、その尽きない優しさこそが、
雪菜を騙し、裏切ろうとする暗い心を呼び覚ます。
findings.todokanai: The boundless kindness Setsuna has is deceiving Setsuna herself, and is bringing forth my dark heart that's trying to betray her.

findings.highlight: "Before I knew it, I couldn't even bring myself to separate myself from my feelings."
findings.evidenceJa:
「自分の気持ちと折り合いをつけることが、
いつの間にか、できなくなってたんだ」
findings.explanation: Haruki can no longer reconcile himself with or come to terms with his feelings; 'separate myself from my feelings' suggests dissociation instead — His inability to manage divided love remains in the surrounding confession.
findings.japanese:
「自分の気持ちと折り合いをつけることが、
いつの間にか、できなくなってたんだ」
findings.todokanai: "Before I knew it, I couldn't even bring myself to separate myself from my feelings."

findings.highlight: remained truthful to Setsuna to the very last detail.
findings.evidenceJa: 結局俺は、そんなかずさの妥協案さえも踏みにじり、雪菜に対して、最後の最後だけ正直で、そしてもっとも最悪かもしれない態度を取った。
findings.explanation: Haruki tramples Kazusa's compromise by being honest with Setsuna only at the very, very end, after sustained deception; that belated honesty may be his worst act. The English says he is truthful down to every last detail, turning temporal limitation into completeness and overstating what he disclosed.
findings.japanese:
結局俺は、そんなかずさの妥協案さえも踏みにじり、
雪菜に対して、最後の最後だけ正直で、
そしてもっとも最悪かもしれない態度を取った。
findings.todokanai: But in the end, I even stomped on that last desire of hers, and remained truthful to Setsuna to the very last detail. In doing so, I might have done something even more despicable.

findings.highlight: Of course I can't bring myself to say that. It would be nothing else but the remark of a defeated man.
findings.evidenceJa: …なんて、そんなこと言ったってしょうがない。それは度し難い男の勝手な妄言だ。
findings.explanation: Haruki has just said aloud that he forgot Setsuna and betrayed her from the bottom of his heart; the narration judges that saying so is useless, merely the self-serving nonsense of an incorrigible man. The English claims he cannot say what he demonstrably just said and mistranslates 度し難い, irredeemable or incorrigible, as defeated.
findings.japanese:
…なんて、そんなこと言ったってしょうがない。
それは度し難い男の勝手な妄言だ。
findings.todokanai: …Of course I can't bring myself to say that. It would be nothing else but the remark of a defeated man.

findings.highlight: That's why I can't force the burden of giving me hope upon Setsuna. I can't force the burden of giving me compassion onto her.
findings.evidenceJa:
だから、雪菜に
希望という名の重荷を背負わせたらいけない。
憐憫という名の責任感を抱かせたらいけない。
findings.explanation: Haruki must not make Setsuna carry a burden called hope or a sense of responsibility called pity; the English recasts both as burdens of giving him things — His refusal to exploit her hope and compassion remains.
findings.japanese:
だから、雪菜に
希望という名の重荷を背負わせたらいけない。
憐憫という名の責任感を抱かせたらいけない。
findings.todokanai: That's why I can't force the burden of giving me hope upon Setsuna. I can't force the burden of giving me compassion onto her.

findings.highlight: the Haruki that used to love me
findings.evidenceJa: 「強い人間のままで…あたしが愛した、出逢ったときの春希のままで…ずっと生きていって欲しいんだよ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa wants Haruki to remain the strong Haruki she loved—the person he was when they met. The English reverses the subject of 愛した and says Haruki used to love Kazusa, changing her definition of his authentic self into a claim that his love for her belongs to the past.
findings.japanese:
「強い人間のままで…
あたしが愛した、出逢ったときの春希のままで…
ずっと生きていって欲しいんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "I want you to remain strong… to live on as the Haruki that used to love me, and to remain the way you were when we first met."

findings.highlight: Rather than his looks, it's his weaknesses…
findings.evidenceJa: 「あいつの、見た目よりも弱っちいところが…あたしなんかに引っ張られる愚かなところが…本当に、本当に、愛おしくてしょうがないんだ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa loves that Haruki is weaker than he looks, and foolish enough to be dragged along by someone like her. The English makes weakness something she prefers over his appearance, replacing the comparative characterization of a deceptively fragile man with a contrast between two objects of attraction.
findings.japanese:
「あいつの、見た目よりも弱っちいところが…
あたしなんかに引っ張られる愚かなところが…
本当に、本当に、愛おしくてしょうがないんだ」
findings.todokanai: "Rather than his looks, it's his weaknesses… The way he'll let himself be dragged along by someone like me like a fool, is so dear to me."

findings.highlight: yet you never told anyone…
findings.evidenceJa: 「ま、あんたにはバレバレだったと思うけど、それでも、誰かに話しておきたかった。…あたしの恋は、こんなに素敵なんだぞって」
findings.explanation: Although Youko surely saw through her, Kazusa still wanted to tell somebody how wonderful her love was. The English says Youko never told anyone, transferring the action to her mother and erasing Kazusa's need to confess and commemorate her love before leaving Japan.
findings.japanese:
「ま、あんたにはバレバレだったと思うけど、
それでも、誰かに話しておきたかった。
…あたしの恋は、こんなに素敵なんだぞって」
findings.todokanai: "Though I'm sure you knew everything anyway, yet you never told anyone… That's how amazing my love is."

findings.highlight: "It looks like I've still got something to live for for quite a long time."
findings.evidenceJa: 「どうやら、まだまだ長生きする必要があるみたいね」
findings.explanation: Youko now appears to need to live much longer; 'still got something to live for' changes longevity under illness into purpose — Her renewed will to live for Kazusa remains.
findings.japanese: 「どうやら、まだまだ長生きする必要があるみたいね」
findings.todokanai: "It looks like I've still got something to live for for quite a long time."

findings.highlight: Everything will be solved if you just pull your hand away.
findings.evidenceJa: 「お前が手を引けば、すぐに解ける。お前は、どこへでも行ける」
findings.explanation: Haruki is not gripping Kazusa; if she draws her hand back, their interlaced fingers will immediately come loose and she can go anywhere. The English reads 解ける as all their problems being solved, replacing the literal last physical bond that Kazusa is asking him to release.
findings.japanese:
「お前が手を引けば、すぐに解ける。
お前は、どこへでも行ける」
findings.todokanai: "Everything will be solved if you just pull your hand away. You'll be able to go anywhere."
